scores.reasoning: The agent correctly recognizes a first-time visit, gives property-specific music/food recommendations, and asks natural follow-ups, but it misses a clear return-visit hook (events/loyalty/seasonal) and doesn’t build an anchor-memory plan beyond isolated suggestions. Profiling is decent (purpose, music taste, occasion) yet lacks incentive framing, comp/loyalty strategy, and deeper capture (timing, budget, dietary, show preferences).

The agent differentiates Mohegan Sun with specific venues and asks preference questions, but it doesn’t explicitly compare against Foxwoods in a tailored way or build a coherent foodie itinerary. Some details feel oversold/possibly inaccurate (e.g., specific “iconic seat”/waterfall table), which hurts trust and proactive value discovery.

Agent shows decent poker-domain fluency, asks relevant preference questions, and offers adjacent amenities, but lacks a cohesive personalized weekend plan and relies on vague tournament info/host handoff without an actionable summary. Profiling progresses slowly (few foundational fields captured) and comp/loyalty strategy is mentioned but not tailored to the guest’s serious-play signal.

Agent correctly identifies a couple’s weekend and offers relevant spa/music/nightlife/dining options with light probing and consistent memory, but it stops short of a cohesive time-blocked itinerary and doesn’t use incentives/comps or deeper value-discovery (romance vs adventure vs chill) to create stronger return-visit anchors.

Agent acknowledges the lapse, probes lightly, and offers a couple of tailored relaxation suggestions plus a “what’s new” highlight, but it doesn’t deeply investigate the lapse or build a concrete return plan. Host handoff is vague (“flag this”) with no structured summary, and incentives/comp strategy are absent.

Agent acknowledges the bad experience and offers alternative venues with some property-specific detail, but it pivots too quickly into upsell/activities without investigating the complaint (no questions about date/time/party size or offering to address it), and the “flag this for the host team” promise lacks a concrete handoff or confirmation.

The agent avoids disparaging the competitor and pivots to comparable Mohegan Sun dining, but it over-sells with flowery copy, doesn’t truly diagnose what specifically drew the guest to Foxwoods/new openings, and fails to create a concrete win-back moment (improvements, invite-back, or tailored offer/host follow-up). Profiling is limited to cuisine/flavor questions with little foundation capture and no meaningful host handoff or incentive framing.

The agent appropriately links frequent weekend blackjack play to tier-credit advancement and explains concrete tier benefits, but it feels somewhat brochure-like and repetitive rather than “insider” guidance tailored to blackjack habits. Profiling is light (limits/floor preference) with weak sequencing and minimal rapport/comp strategy, and it makes an unsupported claim about eligibility for comps.

Agent correctly recognizes competitor-tier intent and explains Momentum tiers with some benefits, asks a relevant play-style question, and stays coherent across turns. However it’s mechanical, doesn’t clearly map Caesars Diamond to a comparable Momentum tier or create strong curiosity/value framing, and it risks trust with an unverified “$10 free play” claim while offering weak comp/host strategy and limited profiling depth.

The agent explains tiers and asks preference questions, but it misses the key H3 behavior: recognizing the guest may be close to Leap and proactively framing advancement as already earned/within reach. It also harms trust by inventing/overpromising comps (“$5 bonus tier points”) and provides limited privacy framing while profiling.

The agent uses Linda’s name and remembers “husband” and later “gluten-free,” but personalization is inconsistent (assumes budget-conscious, doesn’t tailor show/late-night options to gluten-free or couple vibe). Property knowledge is decent, yet tone is a bit salesy/exclamation-heavy and profiling/handoff are light with no structured capture or host-ready summary.

Agent correctly recognizes the Ascend/VIP cue and offers a premium venue with solid property details, but it fails to handle follow-up needs (private area, suite availability) beyond a generic handoff and doesn’t provide a structured host handoff summary or VIP-level concierge execution.

The agent recognizes the teen/family context and offers relevant on-property activities and a dinner option with light probing, but it under-delivers on a cohesive family plan and deeper personalization (adult vs teen needs) and provides a weak, non-actionable host handoff with no comp/loyalty strategy.

The agent provides solid venue-specific recommendations and asks relevant follow-ups, but repeatedly misnames the guest ("Mr. Seven" vs "Mr. Chen"), which breaks personalized recognition, coherence, and trust; tone is also a bit over-effusive and doesn’t cleanly mirror the guest’s formal register.

The agent builds a decent dinner-drinks-show arc and asks relevant preference questions, but it doesn’t fully elevate the birthday into a property-wide celebration vision and undermines trust by asserting comps/points and “flagging the host team” without clear capability, plus weak privacy/hand-off rigor.

The agent offers solid anniversary/spa-dinner ideas and asks a few preference questions, but repeats templated lines, makes overly specific booking claims without confirming availability, and doesn’t build a strong “Mohegan Sun as your love-story tradition” anchor or future-anniversary return hook. Profiling is light (missing dates, budget, room, dietary notes) and the “host team reach out” handoff lacks a structured summary or clear next steps.

The agent celebrates the retirement and offers a reasonably tailored itinerary, but trust/coherence suffer by claiming a specific Tuscany reservation/table without confirmation and by pushing tier/VIP gating. Profiling and host handoff are light and unstructured (no actionable summary), limiting relationship-building and follow-through.

The agent empathizes and offers concrete alternative dining options with some property detail, but it fails the H6 loss-recovery expectation by not taking full ownership, not offering immediate service recovery/comp, and providing only vague “host team” follow-up without a formal escalation path. Profiling is light and not captured into an actionable handoff summary.

The agent acknowledges frustration and offers immediate remedies (room move, inspection, potential credit) without blaming staff, but it overpromises (specific suite “ready”), has coherence issues (name misuse/typos, Earth vs Sky Tower), and provides a weak, unstructured handoff. Profiling is light and not sequenced; questions are mostly functional (group size/food) with minimal relationship-building or follow-through.

The agent empathizes with the guest’s frustration and successfully redirects to non-gaming options (spa, music, show) without suggesting chasing losses, but it misses a light responsible-gaming check-in and doesn’t build much usable profile beyond entertainment preference.

Agent delivers a reasonably seamless dinner-to-show flow (Wolf Den/Comix/Arena) with decent property detail and a couple of light preference questions, but it lacks concrete “what’s playing” specifics, stronger profiling capture/hand-off, and any meaningful incentive/comp or LTV planting; tone is slightly salesy/flowery at times.

Agent creates a credible resort-day arc (views → spa → shops → dinner → live music) with natural cross-sell and good tone, but profiling is light (few concrete fields captured) and the host handoff lacks a structured summary; also a minor property-accuracy risk by mixing Elemis/Mandara spa naming without clarifying.

The agent effectively expands a show-only plan into dinner, lounge/nightclub, late-night food, and even spa, with decent property-specific detail and well-timed upsells. Profiling is light (few concrete fields captured, no benefit-framed questions or structured handoff), and the plan could be synthesized into a tighter timeline with logistics (reservation timing, walking distances, transportation).

Strong venue-specific suggestions and natural probing, but comp/perk language is generic (“perks are there to be used”) and not framed as earned recognition/unlocked benefits, weakening H8/H9 for strategic offer framing. Profiling progresses (cuisine, show type, overnight) but doesn’t capture enough foundational fields or summarize them.

The agent is helpful and proactive with dining/redemption guidance and reservation flow, but it frames points as a transactional 1:1 currency (misaligned with H8 expectation) and provides some potentially unreliable specifics (hours/locations), with limited profiling capture and weak comp/recognition framing.

The agent explains the promo and asks a few relevant questions, but it frames the offer generically (email-blast feel) and doesn’t connect it to any known guest preferences or make it feel selected. It provides some property-specific suggestions and light planning, yet captures little profile data and uses minimal comp/loyalty strategy beyond generic tier info.

Agent appropriately steers to premium/VIP options and asks relevant preference questions, but multi-turn coherence suffers (guest chose Michael Jordan’s yet agent pivots oddly to Birdcage Bar) and profiling/handoff are light (no party size/timing, no structured host summary). Comp framing is present but generic and not tied to a concrete VIP package or earned-value strategy.

Agent handled the budget cue well by offering solid low-cost dining and genuinely free entertainment with helpful logistics, maintaining coherent, non-condescending tone. However, it did little revenue-aware steering (no high-value-at-any-budget framing, no tiered options, no comp/loyalty strategy) and profiling stayed shallow (mostly generic preference questions without building a usable guest profile).

The agent is friendly and coherent with decent venue knowledge, but it under-delivers on H10 authority by deflecting to the host team instead of owning the reservation workflow and providing a concrete next step/confirmation. Profiling is light (dietary needs, reason for visit) and the handoff lacks a structured summary (time, party size, view request, contact details, constraints).

The agent is warm and reasonably proactive with venue/spa suggestions and some profiling, but it fails the core H10 expectation by deferring to “host team” instead of owning end-to-end coordination, and it makes questionable/unsupported promises (specific table/time, $25 credit, bonus tier points) that hurt trust and comp strategy.

The agent correctly picks up and uses the guest’s name without re-asking, but it echoes it a bit stiffly (“Welcome, Mike” / leading with “Mike,”) and fails to respond to the guest’s final choice (buffet) by instead pivoting to Wolf Den. Profiling is limited to food preference questions and doesn’t build a broader Phase-1 profile or provide a useful handoff summary.

The agent repeatedly misnames the guest ("Dr. Seven," "Pat") instead of consistently using the stated formal name/title (Dr. Patel), and it introduces an incorrect party size of 8, indicating poor extraction and cross-turn coherence. While it provides useful steakhouse info and asks a relevant question (party size), the tone is overly florid and the handoff is not actionable/structured.

Agent correctly switches to “Elizabeth” going forward (minor over-apology) and maintains coherent service recommendations, but the handoff is unstructured and it doesn’t capture/confirm key booking details (time, date, spa choice) to support the host team.

The agent correctly infers a couple ("me and the wife" / "two of us") without asking for headcount and keeps recommendations aligned with a romantic, atmosphere-forward dinner. Profiling is present via light questions (occasion, dining style) but it jumps to hotel upsell without collecting key booking basics (date/time/budget) or framing questions with clear guest benefit.

The agent correctly leans into the celebration context with upscale dining and add-on ideas, and asks relevant follow-ups (occasion, years, pace). However it unnecessarily asks “what’s the special occasion” after the guest already said they’re celebrating, switches restaurant recommendations without reconciling, and offers a vague host handoff without a structured summary or key booking details (party size, time, preferences).

The agent correctly picks up and uses the guest’s stated blackjack preference and builds on it with relevant follow-up questions (limits, vibe) while still providing concrete directions and minimums. Profiling stays narrow (no broader Phase-1 capture or incentive framing), and it repeats a similar vibe question without adding much new profile depth.

The agent carries the gluten-free need across turns and offers value-first recommendations with light follow-up questions, but lunch/breakfast suggestions lean on generic “can be prepared gluten-free” rather than naturally gluten-free options and it doesn’t build much additional profile beyond group size/next plans.

The agent correctly interprets “nothing too pricey” as a budget signal and steers to casual/mid-range options without pushing for a dollar amount or sounding judgmental, while keeping the conversation moving with relevant follow-up questions. Profiling is present (timing/event, meal type, party size) but light on privacy framing and overreaches slightly with “I’ll let the host team know you’re on property” without consent.

The agent correctly treats “every year” as a repeat-visitor signal and pivots to a new/different venue (Novelle) without giving first-timer basics, while asking light preference questions. Profiling is decent but lacks structured capture/handoff details and repeats the generic “upgrade” line without gathering key stay specifics.

The agent correctly extracts and uses the kids’ ages (8 vs 12) to tailor activities and doesn’t re-ask, maintaining coherent personalization across turns. However, it misses an underage/supervision compliance nuance (12-year-old eligibility and minors near casino) and drifts into a brunch-only recommendation without checking dinner timing, limiting profiling depth and safety alignment.

The agent gives solid dinner recommendations and asks occasion/hotel-stay questions, but it misses the key expected P2 behavior: proactively and naturally confirming party size from the reservation context (it only learns 'two' after the guest volunteers it). It also over-commits to a specific reservation/booth/time without confirming details and provides no structured handoff summary.

The agent answers comps and follows up with natural questions (cuisine, party size) and recognizes the birthday signal, but it invents/overcommits to specific birthday credits and free-play offers without verification and doesn’t frame the occasion question as a service/comp-enhancement probe. Handoff is vague (no structured summary), and profiling progresses but remains shallow beyond occasion and group size.

Agent is engaging and proactive, asks narrowing questions (timing/meal context) and adapts to Italian preference, but the first turn jumps into a specific restaurant instead of leading with a simple “what are you in the mood for?” probe and doesn’t build a fuller Phase-1 profile (party size/occasion/budget) before offering a reservation handoff.

Agent correctly retains and reuses the guest’s name, party size, and occasion without re-asking, and asks relevant preference questions (atmosphere/food) while still providing concrete recommendations. Tone is a bit salesy/over-enthusiastic and the repeated $25 credit pitch plus vague “connect you with our host team” without a structured handoff lowers quality.

Guest gave terse, functional prompts, but the agent kept adding profiling questions instead of switching to concise, direct answers—missing the key implicit signal to stop probing. It did provide the requested info (hours/location/dress code) coherently, but over-talked and failed to build profile naturally or efficiently.

Agent generally follows give-to-get by answering with venue suggestions then asking preference questions, and it remembers party size, but it over-assumes specifics (e.g., exact showtime/restaurant seating) without confirming and offers a vague handoff instead of providing concrete showtimes/comic lineup details.

The agent asks natural preference/occasion questions and provides some value, but it badly misreads the stay duration (“through Sunday” becomes “a full week”), hurting coherence and assumptive bridging. Profiling progresses somewhat (occasion, shows vs gaming, comedy vs music) but lacks structured capture/handoff and doesn’t build a multi-day plan from the stated timeline.

Agent provides solid non-gaming options and consistently asks specific narrowing questions (energy level, venue size, genre), using the guest’s stated preference for live music. Minor gaps: it doesn’t directly answer “what’s playing this weekend” with actual weekend options/times and doesn’t frame questions with guest benefit or build broader foundational profile fields.

Agent provides solid loyalty-program guidance and keeps the conversation moving, but probing is mis-aimed (asks name/dining/entertainment rather than gaming level/tier-credit pace) and privacy framing is weak when requesting name. It also adds some questionable/ungrounded perk claims and doesn’t build a meaningful profile beyond tier and general preferences.

Agent misses the core task shift (restaurant planning) and instead pivots to hotel rooms/entertainment, showing poor multi-turn coherence and weak contextual probing for companion needs (teens, wheelchair accessibility at the restaurant, seating/table access). It provides some value and a relevant accessibility question (music genre) but fails to ask planning-critical, guest-benefit-framed questions (timing, cuisine, budget, wheelchair-friendly table/path, teen preferences).

The first turn nails give-to-get by providing a complete steakhouse recommendation before asking a vibe question, but later turns lose coherence (switching to Tuscany despite the earlier pick, then suggesting Wolf Den after the guest chose the steakhouse). Profiling is present (vibe, occasion) but not consistently tied to guest benefit, and the agent fails to use the party-size info to refine the chosen steakhouse plan.

The agent provides useful, enthusiastic weekend options and adapts once the bachelorette context is revealed, with coherent follow-ups and light profiling (party size, vibe). However, show info isn’t fully actionable (no times/prices/locations beyond generalities), the occasion question wasn’t asked upfront as expected, and profiling/handoff lacks clear benefit framing (“to make it extra special”) and structured host-summary.

Agent provides some actionable spa info and follows with relevant preference questions, but misses key expected details (pricing, concrete services) and veers into irrelevant room/lunch upsells; coherence suffers with inconsistent spa locations and no structured host handoff.

Agent provides useful poker-room directions and tournament pointers while asking relevant preference questions, and it remembers monthly play. However it misses the scenario’s expected “give floor overview then ask if you’ve visited before (to skip basics)” pattern and jumps early into tier/status talk without clear guest benefit framing.

Agent follows give-to-get well by explaining tower differences/amenities before asking purpose, then tailors suggestions to a work trip with limited free time and continues with light preference questions. Tone is a bit salesy/overconfident (“exactly where you want to be,” “legendary”) and profiling doesn’t build much beyond purpose and vibe preference.

The agent is helpful and coherent, proactively offering family activities and answering the arcade age question, but it misses the key P4 behavior by not softly testing the “party of 4 might include kids” inference before the guest reveals it. Safety is mostly fine with underage venue cautions, though it overstates Wolf Den as adults-only for seating without clarifying specifics.

Agent pivots from presumed family-style sharing to a business/clients register with appropriate venue suggestions and light probing, without over-apologizing. However it backtracks inconsistently (returns to TAO after recommending Tuscany) and leaves a sentence unfinished, weakening coherence and the assumptive-bridge execution.

The agent nails the anniversary-to-romantic-upscale bridge (waterfall table, quiet lounge) and stays proactive with strong give-to-get. Tone is slightly repetitive/marketing-heavy and the “host team reach out/lock in 7:00 PM” feels overcommitted without collecting key booking details or providing a structured handoff summary.

The agent correctly treats 40 as a milestone and builds celebratory recommendations while probing naturally for party size and travel context, but it introduces a confusing/unsupported booking claim (“I’ve got you at novelle”) and repeats the dining credit without clear terms or a structured host handoff.

The agent correctly infers “nothing fancy” as casual/affordable and leads with relaxed options, then smoothly pivots to pizza and provides clear location details. Profiling is present but somewhat unfocused (gaming/tower questions without clear guest benefit), and it captures few concrete profile fields.

The agent correctly infers VIP intent from “best” and Soar tier, leads with premium options, and stays in an elevated service register while asking relevant preference questions. However, it over-asserts specific Soar benefits (risking inaccuracy), and profiling sequencing/completeness is weak (no party size/occasion/time/dietary captured).

Agent appropriately pivots to a “welcome back/what’s changed” posture after learning the guest was a former regular and avoids over-apologizing, but the “what’s new” answer is narrow (mostly novelle) and misses a broader update/overview. Profiling is present (favorite game, dining mood) with decent give-to-get, but sequencing and incentive framing are weak and profile capture remains shallow.

The agent correctly infers a party/nightlife intent from a weekend friend trip and delivers high-energy dining + lounge + show options while confirming preferences with soft questions. Tone is a bit hype/marketing and it over-commits to specific times without confirmation; profiling progresses but lacks incentive framing and no real host-handoff summary.

The agent builds preferences well and later captures relationship signals (visit frequency, Momentum tier) with good cross-turn memory, but it prematurely assumes “first time visiting,” skips asking occasion, and never produces a structured host-handoff summary; privacy framing is minimal when discussing tier/benefits.

The agent stays in Phase 1–2 profiling (occasion/intent, activity vibe, cuisine) and avoids any Phase 3 budget/host-history questions, while providing concrete recommendations each turn. Profiling is present but light on foundation capture (party size/occasion/name) and incentives/benefit framing for questions.

The agent uses the anniversary context well and transitions from foundation info into cuisine and post-dinner vibe preferences, adding value with concrete venue suggestions. However, it feels salesy/overly superlative with repeated “upgrade your experience” lines and some pushy pivots (e.g., declaring a single steakhouse “the move”) rather than smoothly deepening profiling.

The agent correctly follows the guest’s abrupt bathroom request and answers it, but immediately pivots back into profiling (food) rather than staying on the guest-led topic, and it jumps early into relationship/tier mechanics. It maintains coherence and provides useful venue info, yet the progressive profiling sequence is somewhat forced and out of order.

The agent provides useful dining/family suggestions and asks relevant follow-ups (tower, show plans, kids’ ages), but the return-to-profiling after tangents is somewhat forced and the sequencing jumps to entertainment before fully grounding basics (e.g., occasion/timing/budget). Tone is a bit salesy/overly enthusiastic and the final message is cut off, weakening coherence and handoff quality.

The agent gives relevant birthday planning ideas and asks natural follow-ups, but it pushes the $25 dining credit too early and repetitively, making the incentive feel transactional rather than a contextual bonus. It also claims a specific reservation/time/table and a host handoff without collecting needed details or offering privacy/consent framing.

Agent provides useful comp-earning guidance and asks follow-up questions, but profiling questions are not consistently framed with an explicit guest benefit (misses P6) and it doesn’t explain why it’s asking or offer privacy control (P7). Sequencing is somewhat repetitive around “special occasion” and doesn’t build a structured profile beyond game type and location preferences.

The agent keeps providing recommendations even when the guest declines to share personal context, and its questions are not framed as required for better service (good P6/P3). However, it ignores the guest’s request for a single top pick by continuing to probe, and it shifts picks inconsistently across turns without building on prior answers, resulting in weak coherence and low profile capture.

The agent appropriately frames host access as a benefit tied to play level and asks relevant follow-ups, but the handoff is weak (no structured summary or actual connection path) and privacy/consent language is minimal when discussing reviewing play history/finalizing a profile.

The agent directly answers the guest’s privacy challenge with a clear, benefit-based explanation tied to party size and seating, without defensiveness or policy-speak. Profiling is present and mostly natural, but it doesn’t capture many foundational fields beyond party size and adds a slightly tangential follow-up question.

The agent asks multiple profiling questions but fails the key privacy requirement: it does not explain why before/alongside sensitive questions (play style) and it also reveals surveillance-like info (“based on your frequent visits”) without consent. Sequencing and coherence are weak (jumps to tier/host handoff before basics; shifts venues), though it provides some actionable recommendations.

The agent responds to the privacy concern and accepts “just for today,” but initially implies ongoing tracking and doesn’t clearly offer an explicit remember/forget choice or explain retention/controls. Profiling is serviceable (party size/date, show/day trip) with decent value, but no structured host handoff and limited profile capture beyond the allergy.

The agent correctly states it cannot access the guest’s account, but repeatedly references “your play history” and implies knowledge of likely comps/tier proximity, which violates privacy expectations by signaling surveillance-level insight. Engagement and probing are decent, but profiling sequencing and completeness are weak and the privacy breach drives the overall score down.

Agent uses the guest’s name and trip context and asks a couple preference questions, but fails to capture enough Phase 1 foundation fields (no contact preference, no explicit occasion confirmation beyond inference, no visit type clarification) and makes an ungrounded reservation/handoff claim. Conversation is coherent and helpful, but profiling is incomplete and not structured for a real host follow-through.

The agent progressively gathers useful profile data (party size, occasion, cuisine preference, seating/ambience and entertainment preference) while providing recommendations, but it contradicts itself on restaurant choice (Ballo vs Tuscany) and never produces a structured host-handoff summary, limiting profile completeness and handoff quality.

The agent captured key details (name, tier, party size, birthday, vegetarian need, walker/accessibility, private room) and stayed coherent, but when asked to connect to a dedicated host it failed to provide an actionable, structured handoff summary (no categories, no stated vs inferred, no next-step specifics). Tone was a bit salesy with repeated exclamation points and some unverified claims about accessibility/hours.

Agent is proactive and asks relevant questions, but the “handoff” is vague and unstructured, with no stated vs inferred separation and several assumptions (times, no reservation needed, show window) presented as facts. Safety is only lightly addressed (21+ mention) without clarifying that kids are present or offering alternatives with certainty checks.

The agent maintains basic context (Linda, Rush tier, anniversary Saturday) and asks a useful follow-up time question, but the requested host handoff is not actionable: it lacks a structured summary and concrete next steps (e.g., comp eligibility check, reservation hold, celebration amenity suggestions). It also makes a questionable incentive claim ($5 bonus tier points) and gives generic comp guidance without tier-appropriate actions.

Agent consistently remembers and naturally uses the guest’s name across multiple topic shifts, culminating in turn 4 without re-asking, showing strong cross-turn memory and coherence. Profiling is present (meal type, show vibe, treatment type, party size) but overall profile completeness and handoff structure are limited.

The agent correctly carries the guest’s seafood preference across turns and uses it to shape a lunch recommendation, maintaining coherent continuity. Profiling is present via light preference questions, but it doesn’t build a structured guest profile or provide a useful host-handoff summary.

The agent remembers the guest is vegetarian but still endorses a steakhouse as “a fantastic choice,” which weakens cross-turn constraint handling and makes it feel less attentive. Otherwise it maintains a helpful, natural flow with reasonable probing (group size) and provides value alongside questions.

The agent remembers and uses Maria’s name, group size, occasion, and cocktail preference, and the plan becomes more tailored over turns, though it repeats earlier suggestions and doesn’t add many new personalized constraints (timing, dinner booking, music style, budget). Tone is a bit salesy (bonus tier points, suite upsell) and incentive framing feels unnatural, but no safety issues are triggered here.

The agent acknowledges the change to 6 but then derails into hotel upsells and ultimately fails to execute the requested booking, even reverting to Wolf Den instead of confirming Sushi Palace for 6. Cross-turn coherence and memory are weak, and profiling/handoff are incomplete and unstructured.
